question: Under federal law (33 CFR 175.110), which recreational vessels must carry visual distress signals suitable for BOTH day and night use whenever operating on coastal waters, the Great Lakes, and waters connected to the sea?
choice_a: Vessels 26 feet in length or longer
choice_b: Only vessels over 40 feet in length
choice_c: Only vessels carrying six or more passengers
choice_d: Vessels 16 feet in length or longer
explanation: Federal law requires vessels 16 feet or longer (and uninspected passenger vessels regardless of length) to carry visual distress signals suitable for both day and night use.

question: A recreational vessel less than 16 feet in length is required to carry visual distress signals under what circumstance?
choice_a: Only night-use signals, and only when operating between sunset and sunrise
choice_b: Full day and night signals at all times
choice_c: Vessels under 16 feet are completely exempt in all situations
choice_d: Only when operating more than one mile from shore
explanation: Federal law (33 CFR 175.110) requires vessels under 16 feet to carry night-use visual distress signals only when operating between sunset and sunrise.

question: Which of the following is excepted, under 33 CFR 175.115, from the requirement to carry daytime visual distress signals (though it must still carry night signals if operated between sunset and sunrise)?
choice_a: A 24-foot powerboat with an inboard engine
choice_b: A manually propelled boat, such as a canoe or kayak
choice_d: A personal watercraft rented for hire
explanation: Manually propelled boats are excepted from the daytime visual distress signal requirement but must still carry night signals when operated between sunset and sunrise.

question: Under 33 CFR 175.115, an open sailboat with no propulsion machinery aboard is excepted from the daytime visual distress signal requirement if it is under what length?
explanation: An open sailboat under 26 feet in length with no propulsion machinery aboard is excepted from the daytime VDS requirement, but must still carry night signals if operated between sunset and sunrise.

question: A vessel competing in an organized marine parade, regatta, or race is excepted from carrying daytime visual distress signals under 33 CFR 175.115. What must it still carry if it operates at night?
choice_a: Nothing -- it is fully exempt regardless of time of day
choice_b: A full pyrotechnic day/night kit of at least six devices
choice_d: Night-use visual distress signals, if operating between sunset and sunrise
explanation: Vessels competing in an organized marine parade, regatta, or race are excepted from the daytime VDS requirement but must still carry night-use signals if operating between sunset and sunrise.

question: What is the minimum number of federally approved pyrotechnic visual distress devices (such as hand-held red flares) that must be carried aboard a vessel to meet the VDS requirement using pyrotechnics alone?
explanation: A minimum of three pyrotechnic visual distress devices, in any Coast Guard-approved combination meeting the day and/or night requirement, must be carried.

question: Under 33 CFR 175.130, an orange distress flag (approved under 46 CFR 160.072) satisfies which portion of the visual distress signal requirement, and how many must be carried?
choice_a: The night-only requirement; three flags are required
choice_b: The day-only requirement; one flag is required
choice_c: Both day and night requirements; one flag is required
choice_d: It does not satisfy any federal VDS requirement
explanation: An orange distress flag approved under 46 CFR 160.072 satisfies the day-only visual distress signal requirement, and only one is required.

question: Under 33 CFR 175.130, an electric distress light satisfies which portion of the visual distress signal requirement?
choice_a: The day-only requirement; three lights are required
choice_c: The night-only requirement; one light is required
choice_d: It is not a Coast Guard-approved VDS device
explanation: An electric distress light satisfies the night-only visual distress signal requirement, and only one is required.

question: A boater who wants to meet the full-time (day and night) visual distress signal requirement using non-pyrotechnic devices could legally carry which combination?
choice_d: One orange distress flag plus one electric distress light
explanation: One orange distress flag (day-only) together with one electric distress light (night-only) satisfies the full day-and-night visual distress signal requirement.

question: Under 33 CFR 175.320, what is the minimum fire extinguisher requirement for a recreational vessel less than 26 feet in length with no fixed fire extinguishing system aboard?
choice_c: No extinguisher is required regardless of vessel type
explanation: A vessel less than 26 feet in length without a fixed fire extinguishing system must carry at least one 5-B rated portable fire extinguisher.

question: Under 33 CFR 175.320, a vessel 26 feet to less than 40 feet in length, WITHOUT a fixed fire extinguishing system, must carry how many portable fire extinguishers?
choice_b: Two 5-B rated portable fire extinguishers (or one, if a fixed system is installed)
choice_d: None -- only vessels over 65 feet require extinguishers
explanation: A vessel 26 feet to less than 40 feet in length without a fixed fire extinguishing system must carry two 5-B rated portable fire extinguishers; only one is required if an approved fixed system is installed.

question: Under 33 CFR 175.320, how many 5-B rated portable fire extinguishers may one 20-B rated portable fire extinguisher be substituted for?
choice_d: It cannot be substituted for 5-B extinguishers
explanation: One 20-B rated portable fire extinguisher may be substituted for two 5-B rated portable fire extinguishers.

question: Under 33 CFR 175.320, an outboard motorboat less than 26 feet in length may be exempt from carrying a portable fire extinguisher under what condition?
choice_b: If it is operated only on Lake Erie
choice_c: There is no such exemption for any outboard motorboat
choice_d: If its construction will not permit the entrapment of explosive or flammable gases or vapors
explanation: A vessel less than 26 feet in length propelled by an outboard motor is not required to carry portable fire extinguishers if its construction will not permit the entrapment of explosive or flammable gases or vapors.

question: The "B" rating on a marine portable fire extinguisher, such as a 5-B or 20-B unit, indicates it is designed to fight fires involving what?
choice_a: Flammable liquids, such as gasoline, oil, and grease
choice_b: Ordinary combustibles, such as wood and paper
explanation: A Class B rating means the extinguisher is designed for fires involving flammable liquids such as gasoline, oil, and grease -- the type of fire most likely aboard a boat.

question: Under 33 CFR 175.201, which boats are required to be equipped with an operable ventilation system?
choice_a: All boats regardless of engine type or build date
choice_b: Boats built after July 31, 1980, with a gasoline engine used for electrical generation, mechanical power, or propulsion
choice_d: Only boats without an open cockpit
explanation: Federal law prohibits operating a boat built after July 31, 1980, that has a gasoline engine for electrical generation, mechanical power, or propulsion unless it is equipped with an operable ventilation system.

question: Under Inland Navigation Rule 33 (33 CFR 83.33), what sound-signaling equipment must a vessel less than 12 meters (39.4 feet) in length carry?
choice_a: A whistle, bell, and gong, exactly as required for a 100-meter vessel
choice_c: It is not required to carry a whistle or bell, but must have some other means of making an efficient sound signal
choice_d: No sound-signaling means is required at any length
explanation: A vessel less than 12 meters in length is not required to carry the sound-signaling appliances prescribed for larger vessels, but must be provided with some other means of making an efficient sound signal.

question: Under Inland Navigation Rule 33, a vessel 12 meters (39.4 feet) or more in length must carry what sound-signaling equipment, at minimum?
choice_c: No equipment is required until 20 meters
explanation: A vessel 12 meters or more in length must be provided with a whistle.

question: Under Inland Navigation Rule 33, a vessel 20 meters (65.6 feet) or more in length must carry what sound-signaling equipment, at minimum?
choice_a: Both a whistle and a bell
choice_d: No specific equipment beyond what a 12-meter vessel carries
explanation: A vessel 20 meters or more in length must be provided with both a whistle and a bell.

question: Under Inland Navigation Rule 33, a vessel 100 meters or more in length must carry what sound-signaling equipment?
choice_b: A whistle, a bell, and a gong with a tone that cannot be confused with the bell
choice_d: No gong is ever required regardless of length
explanation: A vessel 100 meters or more in length must be provided with a whistle, a bell, and a gong whose tone cannot be confused with that of the bell.
